messages.subject: Measurement invariance number of parameters
parts:
Hello,

I am examining gender invariance with ordered categorical variables in a bifactor model. I am wondering if it is reasonable that the number of parameters in configural model is smaller than that in scalar model and strict model?

I think it shouldn't. The number of parameters should be: configural > scalar > strict? As shown in this paper Measurement Invariance in Longitudinal Bifactor Models: Review and Application Based on the p Factor - Sharon A. S. Neufeld, Michelle St Clair, Jeannette Brodbeck, Paul O. Wilkinson, Ian M. Goodyer, Peter B. Jones, 2024 (sagepub.com)


However, my results showed that the number of parameters in configural, scalar and strict is 466, 517, 471 respectively. What's wrong with it? 

Thank you very much in advance!

Best wishes,
Yuanfei
